summary: Iteration 13 — Backend regression for Phase 3a `PUT /api/mrf/{mrf_id}` draft-edit endpoint + new MRFItem fields (material_id, make/make_id, model/model_id, priority). 15/15 pytest cases PASSED in ~7s against the preview URL. All 14 review-request scenarios green: (1) create with new fields round-trips, (2) SE PUT own draft ok, (3) SE submit→pm_review, (4) PUT after submit→400 'cannot edit after submission', (5) PM /approve action=return→'returned', (6) SE PUT returned→200, (7) different SE (chand@vasuinfosec.com) PUT→403 'creator', (8a) admin PUT draft→200 + (8b) admin PUT after submit→400 (admins do NOT bypass submitted-lock — matches spec), (9) admin project_id change re-snapshots customer_id AND customer_name to the new project's customer, (10) items[] preserves existing item_line_id and generates fresh IDs for new lines, (11) empty body {}→400 'Nothing to update', (12) PM (project member, not creator) PUT draft→403, (13) updated_at refreshes on every PUT, (14) audit_logs contains 'edit_draft' action entry (verified via GET /api/audit?entity_id=<mrf_id>). No product bugs found; no code was modified. Backend-only per request; no frontend testing performed.

minor.issue: If body contains ONLY `project_id` (no other editable key), server returns 400 'Nothing to update' because the `if not updates` guard runs BEFORE the project_id snapshot block (server.py:1365-1378). Test #9 works around this by sending {project_id, site}. If the UI ever emits a lone project_id change, it will incorrectly 400. Recommend moving the project_id resolution above the 'Nothing to update' check, or adding `project_id` to the editable-keys allowlist loop.

action_items: OPTIONAL: In `update_mrf_draft` (server.py:1342-1381) move the `project_id` snapshot block above the `if not updates: raise HTTPException(400, 'Nothing to update')` guard (or seed `updates['project_id']` early) so that a project-only change is accepted. Currently the test suite passes because it always pairs project_id with another field, but a UI that sends only `{project_id: new_id}` will 400.

OPTIONAL (informational): The endpoint intentionally does NOT allow admin/director to override the 'submitted' lock via PUT /api/mrf/{id}. If admins need to fix a submitted MRF, they must use PUT /api/mrf/{id}/items/{line_id} (per-line edit with reason), or PM/GM/Director must first `return` it. Confirm this is the intended UX.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1325-1383 `PUT /api/mrf/{mrf_id}` — status gate (draft|returned) uses both raw and canonical_mrf_status() for defence-in-depth; correct. Error string exactly matches the spec verbiage ('cannot edit after submission (only \'returned\' MRFs can be re-edited)').
server.py:1338-1340 RBAC — creator-OR-admin/director-only. PMs (even when assigned to the project) are correctly blocked from editing SE-authored drafts (test 12).

server.py:1346-1363 items merge — merges old-item dict with new-item dict when item_line_id matches; new items get `mli_<uuid>` (test 10 verified both branches). Sensible default fills for status/billing_status/qty_* counters. `qty_approved` defaults to `qty_requested` when omitted — matches create_mrf semantics.

server.py:1368-1378 project change block — re-fetches project and customer to update `customer_id` + `customer_name` snapshot. Fallback chain: customer.name → project.client → '' (test 9 verified update path to a DIFFERENT customer).
server.py:1365-1378 EDGE CASE — as flagged above, a body containing only `project_id` (no other editable key) will 400 before the snapshot block runs. Low-impact but worth a one-line fix.

server.py:1380-1383 `updated_at = now_utc()` on every successful PUT (test 13 verified >=1s delta) and `audit('edit_draft', ..., {non-items updates})` recorded — visible via GET /api/audit?entity_id=<mrf_id> (test 14).

server.py:193-211 MRFItemIn — new optional fields (material_id, make, make_id, model, model_id, priority) accept null/empty; priority defaults to 'normal'. Round-trip verified via POST /mrf → response items[] (test 1). NOTE: server does NOT validate `priority` values against {low, normal, high, urgent} — an arbitrary string would be persisted as-is. Not tested but flagging for defensive-input hardening.
server.py file size: 3026 lines — repeat of iter-12 note. Consider extracting mrf/po/masters routers for maintainability.
seed_data_creation: Test file creates two isolated projects with distinct customers per test session: TESTCUSTA-<hex>/TP-A-<hex> and TESTCUSTB-<hex>/TP-B-<hex>. Both projects have siteeng@vasu.dev and pm@vasu.dev pre-assigned as site_engineer/project_manager. Each PUT test creates a fresh MRF so tests are independent; every MRF is prefixed 'TEST-Iter13' in item description for easy identification. Fully idempotent — safe to re-run. Uses second SE via chand@vasuinfosec.com (fresh dev-login user auto-created).
